onboarding.project.title: Create your first project
onboarding.project.body: A project is a folder hosting a .backlog/ with your kanban, claims and orchestrator state. You can point at an existing folder or create a new one.
onboarding.repos.title: Add workspaces
onboarding.repos.body: Each run works in a specific workspace: local folder, Git checkout, or remote Git. Add at least one folder before launching agents.
onboarding.task.title: Create your first task
onboarding.task.body: Describe what you want done (e.g. "Refactor billing into its own service"). Backlog will propose an AI split into per-workspace sub-tasks.
onboarding.split.title: Split your task into sub-tasks
onboarding.split.body: Click the ✂ button on the card to open the SplitDialog. The AI proposes 2-6 sub-tasks with scopes, risk and dependencies. You can tweak before applying.
git_status.missing_repo: Workspace not found. Click to relocate it.

create_project.hint.git: Clones remote Git, initializes Backlog in it, and registers the project.
create_project.hint.existing: The folder must already contain a .backlog/ (created via backlog init).
create_project.field.path_help: If the folder does not exist, Backlog creates it, then adds .backlog/ with config and state files.
create_project.field.clone_path_help: Backlog will clone Git there, then create the project state inside it.
create_project.field.path_existing_help: Backlog will look for a .backlog/ at this path and add it to your registry.

card.play_no_agent: No AI agent is enabled on this project. Enable Claude Code or Codex in the Agents section to be able to run this task.
topbar.play_no_todo: No to-do task. Create one with "+ Task" before clicking Play.
preflight.no_agent.title: No AI agent enabled on this project
preflight.no_agent.body: Clicking Play won't run anything until an agent (Claude Code or Codex) is enabled. Configure one to make runs possible.
preflight.no_api_key.title: API key required
preflight.no_api_key.body: Set your Anthropic or OpenAI key to let the agents run. Stored encrypted, never leaves your machine.
preflight.title: Before pressing Play
preflight.body: Backlog checks the visible prerequisites whenever the window opens or becomes active again.
card.play_no_api_key: Set your Anthropic or OpenAI API key first. Opening the dialog now — paste it and try Play again.
card.play_at_capacity: Your agent is already running another task at the same time as the one you just clicked. Wait for it to finish (or stop it via the red ◼ button at the top) before launching this one.
card.play_risk_not_allowed: This task is tagged risk=high but your agent only accepts low/medium-risk work. Either lower the task's risk in its detail panel, or open Agents → claude-code → Allowed risk and tick "high".
card.play_missing_capabilities: This task asks for a capability your agent doesn't claim (e.g. run_tests, git_write). Open Agents → your agent → Capability presets and pick one that covers what the task needs.
card.play_no_repository: No workspace is configured for this project. Add or select a working folder before starting a run.
card.play_repository_missing_checkout: The targeted workspace has no available local folder. Open Workspaces to relocate it or add a usable folder.
card.play_repo_blocked: The workspace this task touches is set to "no-access" or isn't in your agent's allowed list. Open Workspaces → that workspace → switch its access mode back to "read + write".
card.play_detached_head: This Git workspace is on a detached HEAD. Select a branch in Git > Branches, then press Play again.
card.play_missing_executable: Backlog can't find this agent executable from the Desktop app. Check Agents → Command, or install Claude Code / Codex in ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin.
card.play_direct_dirty: This workspace already has local changes. Choose an action to start the task without mixing your edits with the run's edits.
direct_dirty.title: Checkout already has changes
direct_dirty.body: This task is configured for direct mode, but the workspace already has local changes. Backlog refuses this start so the agent does not mix its edits with yours.
direct_dirty.worktree_hint: Backlog keeps your current checkout intact and starts the agent in an isolated copy.
direct_dirty.retry_hint: Commit or stash your local changes in the workspace, then retry in direct mode.
direct_dirty.continue_hint: The agent will work in your current checkout despite the existing changes. If Commit is enabled, those changes may be included in the run commit.
direct_dirty.task_missing: This task is no longer visible on the board. Refresh the project, then try again.
card.play_direct_busy: A direct run is already working in this workspace. Wait for it to finish or stop it before starting another direct run.
card.play_unknown_repo: This task references a workspace that's no longer registered in this project. Either re-add it under Workspaces, or edit the task to point at an existing workspace.
card.play_autonomy_observe: Your project is in "observe" mode — agents only watch, they don't run. Open Settings (left panel) → Autonomy → switch to "assist" or higher.
card.play_manual_approval: This task will wait for manual approval in In Review after the run.
card.play_high_risk: This is a high-risk task and your project's autonomy mode is too low for it. Open Settings → Autonomy → choose "delegate" (manual approve at end) or "autopilot".
card.play_scheduler_capacity: Too many tasks are already scheduled to launch this round. Wait a few seconds for them to start, then click Play again.
card.play_scope_conflict: Another active claim is editing the same files this task would touch. Wait for it to finish (▶ in the activity panel shows what's running), or cancel it.
card.play_waiting_on: This task depends on another sub-task that hasn't finished yet. Open the task's detail panel to see which one — finish or unblock it first.
card.play_dependency_failed: A sub-task this one depends on has failed. Open the task's detail panel, retry the failing dependency, then come back.

create_task.field.title: Title
create_task.field.description_help: Describe what you want done. Be concrete about WHAT and WHERE — the AI will name the task from this.
create_task.field.description_title_hint: Title is generated from this description (verb-led: "Add…", "Fix…", "Update…"). You can rename later from the card.
create_task.title_source.fallback: AI unavailable — used a first-sentence fallback. Rename it from the card if needed.
create_task.assignee.hint: Pick a specific agent or human, or leave Auto for the orchestrator's ranking.
create_task.execution.title: Execution
create_task.execution.auto_split_desc: Ask the AI to propose 2-6 sub-tasks scoped per workspace. Enable only for multi-file or multi-workspace work; leave it off for a simple change.
create_task.execution.manual_approval_de: Run stops in IN REVIEW awaiting your sign-off. Unchecked = the agent commits + completes if the work passes its own checks.
create_task.execution.worktree_note: Runs always execute in an isolated git worktree — your current branch is safe.
create_task.execution.commit_when_done_d: Stage and commit the agent's changes as soon as the run finishes. In direct mode, leaving this off keeps files modified in your checkout.
create_task.execution.push_when_done_des: Push the run's branch to origin so collaborators can see the work. Skipped silently if the Git workspace has no remote.
create_task.execution.create_pr_desc: After push, run `gh pr create` (GitHub today) to open a PR. Skipped with a hint if `gh` isn't installed or authenticated.
create_task.execution.merge_pr_desc: Squash-merge the PR as soon as it's green. If your branch has required CI checks or reviews, the merge waits for them.
create_task.execution.worktree_isolated_: Safe and parallel-friendly — your current branch is never touched.
create_task.execution.worktree_direct_hi: Edits land directly in your working copy. Backlog refuses to start if your branch already has tracked changes.
create_task.git.title: Git
create_task.ai.title: AI split
create_task.ai.auto_split_desc: Ask the selected model to prepare a parallel plan. Off → the task launches as one run.
create_task.ai.subagent_model_hint: Generated sub-tasks will prefer this model when launched.
create_task.ai.default_prompt: Split the task so the work can run in parallel with as few dependencies as possible. Group independent files into balanced batches according to max_subagents. Only add dependencies when one sub-task truly needs another sub-task's output.
create_task.ai.estimate_desc: Run a short LLM call before scheduling to ballpark how long the task will take. Off by default — historical data takes over after a few runs anyway.
create_task.clarify.body: This request can be interpreted in multiple ways. Clarify it before creating the task.
create_task.clarify.question.naming: How should generated files be named?

integrations.github.oauth.guide.title: Connect your own GitHub OAuth App
integrations.github.oauth.guide.subtitle: 5 minutes, no Backlog Cloud account needed. If you have one, close this panel — connection happens on its own.
integrations.github.oauth.guide.step1.ti: 1. Create an OAuth App on GitHub
integrations.github.oauth.guide.step1.bo: You'll be redirected to github.com/settings/applications/new in a new tab. You must be signed in to your GitHub account.
integrations.github.oauth.guide.step3.ti: 3. Submit and copy the Client ID
integrations.github.oauth.guide.step3.bo: Once the app is created, GitHub shows the Client ID at the top of the page (starts with Iv1. or Ov23li…). Copy it.
integrations.github.oauth.client_id_help: Create an OAuth App (Enable Device Flow ☑️) and paste its Client ID here.
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.title: Connect your own Atlassian OAuth App
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.subtitle: 10 minutes, no Backlog Cloud account needed. With a Backlog account it's zero-config — sign in on the Account tab.
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.step1.body: On developer.atlassian.com → Create → OAuth 2.0 integration. Pick a name (e.g. Backlog) and accept the terms.
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.step2.body: In the left menu, make sure "Distribution" is set to Private. You can switch to Public later to share with other Atlassian accounts.
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.step3.body: "Permissions" menu → click "Configure" on Jira API and check at least:
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.step4.body: "Authorization" menu → OAuth 2.0 (3LO) → "Configure" → paste this Callback URL:
integrations.jira.oauth.guide.step5.body: "Settings" menu → copy the Client ID and the Secret (click "Show secret" to reveal), then paste them here.
integrations.jira.oauth.help: Create an OAuth App on developer.atlassian.com with scopes read:jira-work, read:jira-user, offline_access and redirect_uri = {redirect}.
integrations.github.cloud_optional: Backlog Cloud is optional. You can connect GitHub locally with the Device Flow below or with a token.
integrations.jira.jql_placeholder: project = ABC AND status != Done order by updated desc
